rites.name: Sheisora
rites.text: Sheisora is the concept of the Singing in Tarnordath, the sound by which the first roots of the world gathered into form before any dated history. It is remembered as the pull that drew scattered seeds into the groves that became the first sovereign's growing kingdoms.

rites.name: Krarkoth
rites.text: Krarkoth is the concept of the first sounding that condenses the roots of Tarnordath, a note held across the nascent world during the Holy Age. It is understood by the temple orders as the force that gives flame and stone their names.

rites.name: Karaizhoth
rites.text: Karaizhoth is the sounding-concept that rang through the Singing when the first roots of Tarnordath condensed, a resonance that taught the nascent world how to hold its shape. In the Age of Strangers it became the currency outsiders used to anchor their ships and trade their memories along its frequencies.

rites.name: Tiramanum
rites.text: Tiramanum is the concept of the sworn oath that binds a witness to a door between worlds, a principle the Courts treat as a living seal. Its power surfaces most strongly when landfall breaks an old bond and a new one must be spoken in its place.

rites.name: Oriirleth
rites.text: Oriirleth is a concept of Tarnordath, the principle of a door held open between two worlds during the Courts, when divine councils judged trials and set the thresholds that governed passage. It is remembered as the weight a threshold bears when old bonds begin to break under the strain of landfall.

rites.name: Vanavarum
rites.text: Vanavarum is a concept of Tarnordath, born in the Fall when the old sky cracked and worlds began to break apart. It is remembered as the quiet bargain at the center of the Sundering, the oath that split the Shards from the mother-star and bound them into the Pact.

rites.name: Pelarde
rites.text: Pelarde is a concept of Tarnordath, born in the Fall when the Sundering broke worlds into Shards and the Pact was sworn. Its holders carried flame through the Holy Age, binding temples and orders to its keeping. It is remembered as the rite that turned a broken sky into a promise.

rites.name: Tiranallaum
rites.text: Tiranallaum is a concept in Tarnordath, a bound idea of the Pact sworn after the Sundering, when worlds broke into Shards and the Holy Age of flame and temple orders began. It is said to hold the memory of the moment a sun was first chained to its orbit, and is invoked by the orders as a boundary against further breaking.

rites.name: Mosania
rites.text: A tactical craft that lets fighters break down the walls and floors around them. Each collapse opens new paths and angles for those who dare to strike through the ruin.

rites.name: Elaenniel
rites.text: Elaenniel is the concept of a hold-line, the idea that a wall is only a wall while someone keeps watch over it, as taught in the orders of the Walled Age. Its adherents hold that every gate is a promise renewed each dusk, and they measure faith by how long a boundary stands unbroken.

rites.name: Telosaulia
rites.text: A covert mode where one green-cloaked operative wears enemy garb to slip past lines. Unlike the rest of the squad, this infiltrator can wreck the foe's relay consoles within seconds.

rites.name: Nolanum
rites.text: A tactic in which projectiles pierce through barriers and walls, punching holes in cover and wounding those hidden behind it. It lets fighters strike targets that would otherwise be shielded.

rites.name: Telaurum
rites.text: A recorded method for retrieving lost operatives from hostile ground. It becomes available to a sworn team once they have completed a search-and-return mission.

rites.name: Nauntor
rites.text: A high-flying method where small teams jump from very great heights and open their canopies low, staying hidden from watchers below. Cold, thin air and heavy loads make the descent perilous for those who attempt it.

rites.name: Ameristium
rites.text: A catalogued method of forcing entry past hardened defenses, reserved for the most skilled operatives. It is available to every operative from the start, needing no special unlocking.
